hints.content:
A figure has **rotational symmetry** if there is a rotation that maps the figure onto itself.

Any line segment in the figure would have to map onto a congruent line segment in the same figure.  

Further, the segment lengths and angles between them must repeat in the same order around the center.

The **magnitude** of the rotation is the number of degrees we can rotate the figure to map it onto itself.

Will the rhombus map onto itself with $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ rotations about the origin?

Let's check the rotation of $90^\circ$ about the origin.

Some points on the rhombus map to points which are not on the figure. So the rhombus does **not** have rotational symmetry at a magnitude of $90^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A rhombus mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center of the rhombus is at the origin. A pre-image rhombus has a point at negative eight, negative four, a point at negative two, four, a point at two, negative four, and a point at eight, four. The image rhombus has a point at negative four, negative two, a point at negative four, eight, a point at four, two, and a point at four, negative eight. An arc shows the pre-image was rotated ninety degrees to form the image.

hints.content:
Let's check the rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin.

The figure maps onto itself, so it is **symmetric** about the origin at a $180^\circ$ magnitude of rotation.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A rhombus mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center of the rhombus is at the origin. A pre-image rhombus has a point at negative eight, negative four, a point at negative two, four, a point at two, negative four, and a point at eight, four. An arc shows the pre-image was rotated one hundred eighty degrees to form the image mapped onto the pre-image.

hints.content:
This is the completed table:

Rotation | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Rotational symmetry of $90^\circ$ about the origin | No
Rotational symmetry of $180^\circ$ about the origin | Yes
